rationale: I'm replacing Fisher-z Pearson correlations with a Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage covariance per subject, projected into Riemannian tangent space at the group's geometric mean. In large benchmarks (Dadi et al. 2019) this was the most reliable connectivity measure for rs-fMRI diagnosis. Shrinkage makes estimates more stable with short, site-varying scans. The tangent projection centers out shared structure and keeps covariance geometry, which tends to reduce site and subject noise. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

ADHD prevalence differs sharply by sex (mostly boys), age and site recruitment, and none of these is in the current connectivity-only model. Stacking fixes that: an inner-CV out-of-fold tangent-space logistic-regression score is combined with sex, age and site one-hot in a small second-stage logistic regression, so the covariates aren't drowned out by about 20k strongly regularized connectivity features.

Instead of mapping every subject at one shared geometric mean, I re-centre each site's covariances onto its own geometric mean before taking the matrix log. This is Riemannian re-centring, which removes scanner and protocol shifts in connectivity, the dominant nuisance across the 8 ADHD-200 sites, so the classifier works on within-site differences. Site base rates are still handled by the site one-hot in the stacker. The step only uses site labels and is label-free; sites with very few subjects fall back to the global mean. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

I'm adding a second, anatomically defined parcellation (AAL, 116 ROIs) next to the functional CC200. Each atlas gets the same per-site re-centred tangent pipeline and its own L2 logistic regression. Their out-of-fold scores are stacked with sex, age and site. Different parcellations capture complementary views of the connectome, and ensembling across atlases is a reliable gain in rs-fMRI benchmarks (Dadi et al. 2019; Abraham et al. 2017). AAL also adds whole-cerebellum and subcortical coverage, which is relevant to ADHD's fronto-striatal-cerebellar circuitry, and it is cheap to compute. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

Z-scoring each series before the shrinkage covariance throws away regional signal amplitude, which approximates ALFF because the data are already band-pass filtered. Abnormal ALFF in frontal, striatal and cerebellar regions is a well-replicated rs-fMRI finding in ADHD (Zang et al. 2007). This change adds a second, low-dimensional stream: per-ROI log amplitude relative to the subject's global mean (mALFF-style normalisation) plus the global level. Each column is z-scored within site, without labels. The stream gets its own L2 logistic regression, and its inner-CV out-of-fold score is stacked with the connectivity score and the sex, age and site covariates. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

ADHD-200 sites recruited cases and controls very differently. Some sites' ADHD groups are almost all boys, and age ranges differ by site. So a single global sex effect and a single global age effect, added to site intercepts, misstate the demographic base rates. This change adds site×sex and site×(centred age) interaction terms to the second-stage logistic stacker, so each site gets its own sex and age effect, with mild extra regularisation (C=0.5) to offset the added columns. The connectivity pipeline is unchanged. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

The connectivity logistic regression's C=0.001 was fixed by hand. Round 3's per-site re-centring removed most of the site signal from the tangent features, so the right amount of regularisation has probably changed. This version picks C from a log grid (1e-4 to 1e-2) on the training fold, using the grouped inner CV that already exists. It reuses the winning C's out-of-fold scores as the stacker input, so the cost is small.

Per-site Riemannian re-centring lines up each site's mean connectivity, but sites still differ in spread: scan length, TR and noise change how widely subjects scatter around their site mean in tangent space. That is the "scale" half of ComBat, and the current model leaves it uncorrected. This change standardises each tangent feature within site, label-free, shrinking each site's variance toward the pooled within-site variance (prior weight of 10 subjects) so small sites stay stable, which keeps noisier sites from dominating the shared classifier. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

Connectivity in children and adolescents changes strongly with age and differs by sex. ADHD-200 sites also differ in their age and sex mix between cases and controls, so the tangent features probably carry a lot of developmental and sex variance. The stacker then partly double-counts that variance instead of seeing what connectivity adds on top. This change removes age, age² and sex from every tangent feature by a pooled linear regression, after the per-site re-centring and scaling. The covariates are centred within each site and no labels are used. The connectivity score then measures how far a subject's connectome sits from what is expected for their age and sex (a "maturational lag"-style signal), and the stacker still models age and sex directly.

This changes the parcellation from CC200 (~200 regions) to CC400 (~392 regions), keeping the same per-site re-centring, tangent projection, site scaling and stacking. The idea is that finer regions separate sub-networks that CC200 averages together, such as fronto-striatal, dorsal-attention and cerebellar parcels. In large rs-fMRI diagnosis benchmarks, higher resolution plus tangent space tends to help. To fit the time limit, each L2 logistic regression is trained on a compressed version of the training matrix (its SVD), which gives exactly the same solution. The per-site geometric means use 8 iterations instead of 30, and the whole-pool fallback mean is a simpler log-Euclidean mean.
